classification.difficultyReason: Calculate missing angles, including isosceles base angles, and compare corresponding angles to establish or reject similarity.

content.prompt: By using the angle sum of a triangle, decide if the given pairs of triangles are similar.

spec.description: Two triangles side by side, the left with a horizontal lower side and the right with a horizontal upper side. Ordinary source blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: Left given angles: 100 degrees at lower left and 45 degrees at lower right. Right given angles: 35 degrees at upper left and 100 degrees at upper right. Coordinates reproduce orientation without asserting scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles are visible; missing angles and the similarity decision belong to answers.

answer.short: Yes. Both triangles have angles $35^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $100^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Missing angle}&=180^\circ-100^\circ-45^\circ\\&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$
Right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Missing angle}&=180^\circ-35^\circ-100^\circ\\&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
The triangles are similar because at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).

spec.description: Two right triangles side by side in opposite orientations, retaining both right-angle squares. Ordinary outlines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: Left right angle at lower left and 38 degrees at upper left. Right right angle at upper right and 62 degrees at upper left.
spec.answerVisibility: Missing angles and the negative similarity decision are absent from the student diagram.

answer.short: No. The angle sets are $38^\circ,52^\circ,90^\circ$ and $28^\circ,62^\circ,90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Missing angle}&=180^\circ-90^\circ-38^\circ\\&=52^\circ\end{align*}$$
Right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Missing angle}&=180^\circ-90^\circ-62^\circ\\&=28^\circ\end{align*}$$
Only the right angles match. There are not two pairs of equal corresponding angles, so the triangles are not similar.

spec.description: An upward isosceles triangle with double side ticks beside a smaller downward isosceles triangle with single side ticks.
spec.mathematics: Left equal sloping sides and 81 degrees at the lower-left base. Right equal sloping sides and 28 degrees at the lower apex. Tick styles distinguish the equal-side pairs within each triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: The other angles and the similarity decision are answer-only.

answer.short: No. The angle sets are $81^\circ,81^\circ,18^\circ$ and $76^\circ,76^\circ,28^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The base angles of each isosceles triangle are equal.
Left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Apex angle}&=180^\circ-2\times81^\circ\\&=18^\circ\end{align*}$$
Right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Each base angle}&=\frac{180^\circ-28^\circ}{2}\\&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
The corresponding angles are not equal, so the triangles are not similar.

spec.description: A right-pointing isosceles triangle with a vertical base and double side ticks beside an upward isosceles triangle with single side ticks.
spec.mathematics: Left equal sides meet at the right apex; lower-left base angle is 37.5 degrees. Right equal sloping sides meet at an apex of 105 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle labels are visible; calculated angles and the affirmative decision belong to answers.

answer.short: Yes. Both triangles have angles $37.5^\circ$, $37.5^\circ$ and $105^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The base angles of each isosceles triangle are equal.
Left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Apex angle}&=180^\circ-2\times37.5^\circ\\&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
Right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Each base angle}&=\frac{180^\circ-105^\circ}{2}\\&=37.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
The triangles are similar because at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).
